transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-23 14:00 PDT, Duration 42 minutes. Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam O'Neill, Samir Patel (Redwood); Priya Rao, Ethan Morales, Diana Lopez, Marco Nguyen (Acorn Systems)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, appreciate you carving out time. I'm Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on this deal, and with me are Liam, our solutions engineer and Samir on product.
[00:12] Priya Rao: Hi Maya, thanks. Priya here, head of search at Acorn. We have Ethan and Diana on, and Marco. We're excited to see the embeddings + rerank flow.
[00:19] Liam O'Neill: Cool, we'll go through a short agenda — quick context, API demo for embeddings, then the reranker endpoint and Console for routing/rollouts, finally Optimize suggestions for cost/latency. Feel free to stop and ask.
[00:30] Ethan Morales: Quick context from our side: we power product and docs search across 50 million content items, average query loads peek at about 350 qps, and latency SLO for query + rerank is 200ms P95. We're currently using an in-house late-binding reranker and Elasticsearch for retrieval.
[00:46] Samir Patel: Helpful. When you say late-binding, is the rerank within the same request path or async?
[00:51] Ethan Morales: Synchronous, so it impacts our tail. We're seeing cost creep and some variance in latencies during peak.
[00:58] Liam O'Neill: Got it. So maybe Hosted API with prefix caching and selective batching could give a good tradeoff for cost while meeting latency. We'll demo how the Redwood embeddings endpoint plus the reranker endpoint can slot into your existing ES top-K+rerank pattern.
[01:15] [screen share begins — Console]
[01:18] Liam O'Neill: Alright, Console view here — model catalog on the left, you can see verified performance profiles. I'm launching a quick request to the embeddings endpoint, note the model variant and quantization toggle — some of these names get garbled by the transcription, but that's the Optimize panel over on the right.
[01:33] Marco Nguyen: That Optimize thing — is that an automated recommender? We want specific batch sizes tuned for our QPS distribution.
[01:39] Samir Patel: Right, Optimize suggests batching and KV/prefix caching params based on your traffic histogram. For example, if you have many short queries (<= 64 tokens) it'll recommend smaller batch windows to keep latency low; for heavy tails it suggests warm-KV cache sizes.
[01:52] [01:55] Priya Rao: Can you explain the reranker endpoint? How is it different from calling the embeddings endpoint and scoring locally?
[02:02] Liam O'Neill: Sure — two common patterns. One, you call embeddings for query/doc vectors and do an ANN search then local scoring. Two, call Redwood reranker endpoint which takes top-K candidate ids + optionally the raw text and returns pairwise scores or a ranked list. The reranker is optimized to operate with KV cache for the model's kv, so repeated doc prefixes are cheaper.
[02:26] Ethan Morales: How do you handle tokenization differences? We saw misalignments with other vendors where tokens changed across models.
[02:33] Samir Patel: Good point — we version the model and provide a model spec that includes tokenizer fingerprint; you can pin model version in the Console to avoid drift during rollouts. That avoids a silent token mismatch.
[02:44] [03:00] Diana Lopez: From security, we need SOC2 Type II, support for SAML SSO, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Also network: can you support VPC peering, or do you require public endpoints?
[03:13] Maya Chen: Yes — we have SOC2 docs and network diagram. For Hosted we offer private networking options — VPC peering for dedicated; with Hosted we typically use customer-controlled egress and TLS with customer-managed keys for sensitive workloads. We'll share the security pack after this call.
[03:28] Diana Lopez: And data retention? We need assurance that customer content isn't used to train upstream models.
[03:33] Liam O'Neill: For Hosted commercial customers we have an opt-out for data usage — we persist only for telemetry and a short troubleshooting window unless you opt-in. We'll include that in the security docs.
[03:44] [04:00] Liam O'Neill: Now demo time — I'll hit the embeddings endpoint with a sample product query. Sending...
[04:06] [04:10] Speaker 2: Embedding call returns vector, about 12ms on this test, dot product to our local ANN returns top-20 candidates. Then we POST to the reranker endpoint with a JSON payload of candidates and the user query.
[04:25] Liam O'Neill: The reranker can return either scores per candidate or a fully re-ranked list. Here I'll show the pairwise score mode, which lets you tune downstream thresholding.
[04:36] Marco Nguyen: Is the payload size a concern? We send long product descriptions sometimes — 2-3k tokens per doc.
[04:44] Samir Patel: For long docs we recommend storing precomputed embeddings and sending doc ids to the reranker with the default excerpt or small summary. The reranker can fetch cached doc prefix KV entries if you enable prefix caching in the Console. That reduces repeated long-token costs.
[04:59] [05:15] Priya Rao: Can I see cost estimates? For our dataset and 350 qps peak, what's the rough per-token cost vs our current infra?
[05:23] Liam O'Neill: We ran a rough calc earlier — with dynamic batching and a warm KV cache we estimate 40-55% lower cost per ranked query compared to a full-text model rerank on large documents. I'll follow up with an itemized cost sheet.
[05:38] [05:55] Ethan Morales: Latency — you mentioned P95 200ms target. Does Redwood hosted API include SLOs? What about Dedicated?
[06:03] Maya Chen: Hosted has published latency profiles per model; Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and tighter SLOs. For your 200ms P95, we think a hosted configuration with small batch windows and prefix caching should work but we recommend a pilot to validate with your real traffic shape.
[06:21] [06:40] Liam O'Neill: I'll pull up a trace example in the Console — here's a sample end-to-end trace: query arrives, embeddings call 12ms, ANN local step 4ms, reranker request 70ms P95 on this model variant, total 86ms not counting network. Those numbers will be different at scale and region; again, pilot will give real numbers.
[06:58] Marco Nguyen: What about model variants and quantization — are some variants faster but lower quality?
[07:04] Samir Patel: Yes, we expose multiple variants: full fp16, int8-quantized, and trimmed layers for smaller latency. Optimize recommends a quantization profile based on your eval set: it shows estimated delta in ranking metrics vs speedup.
[07:18] [07:35] Priya Rao: Can we run an eval with our own relevance labels? We have annotated query sets.
[07:42] Liam O'Neill: Absolutely — we can ingest your test set into a sandbox and run A/B comparisons across model variants and reranker thresholds. That feeds directly into Optimize's regression alerts.
[07:54] Diana Lopez: For legal/procurement, licensing — any vendor lock-in? And can we export logs and telemetry?
[08:02] Maya Chen: No vendor lock-in — you can pin models, and you always retain your vectors and logs. We provide exports for audit and telemetry. For Dedicated/Private you control more of the control plane.
[08:14] [08:30] Ethan Morales: Okay, talk me through a simple integration: we keep ES for retrieval, call embeddings for query, nearest neighbor, then pass top-20 ids to Redwood reranker — how's the SDK look?
[08:41] Liam O'Neill: SDKs are in Python, Node, and Java. Example: call client.embeddings.create(query), then client.rerank.score({candidates: [ids], query}). We also have a streaming option if you want progressive scoring. There's a code snippet in the Console under 'Quickstarts' that I can share.
[09:00] [09:12] Priya Rao: Are there throttles and rate limits that might impact burst behavior?
[09:18] Samir Patel: Hosted initially has per-tenant rate limits but we tune them for pilots. For production, we recommend Dedicated or reserved throughput if bursts are sustained. Console shows rate limit usage and per-route dashboards.
[09:33] [09:45] Marco Nguyen: A nit — you mentioned KV cache and prefix caching — what's the memory footprint estimate per doc?
[09:51] Liam O'Neill: It's workload-dependent, but as a rule of thumb prefix entries per doc are small — store only the first N tokens or a canonical excerpt you configure. Optimize will recommend a cache size tradeoff; for your corpus we estimate a warm prefix cache of ~50GB for top-500k docs would yield strong hit rates.
[10:12] [10:30] Diana Lopez: Back to compliance: you mentioned customer-managed keys. Is HSM supported?
[10:36] Maya Chen: Yes, we integrate with common KMS/HSM providers for key wrapping. We'll include specifics in the security pack.
[10:46] [11:00] Liam O'Neill: Alright, last part — rollouts. Console supports canary deploys and automatic fallback rules. If a model variant fails quality checks or latency thresholds, traffic automatically falls back to the previous stable variant.
[11:14] Priya Rao: That fallback is critical for us. Can we define quality checkpoints based on our eval metrics?
[11:20] Samir Patel: Yes, you can tie regression alerts to your eval suite; if NDCG drops beyond threshold, it triggers rollback.
[11:27] [11:40] Ethan Morales: Anything about egress/data residency? We have EU-only data for some customers.
[11:46] Maya Chen: We have region controls and can pin workloads to EU regions for data residency. For stricter needs we can talk about Private deployment.
[11:55] [12:10] Priya Rao: Ok quick recap?
[12:14] Maya Chen: Recap — Redwood Hosted API: embeddings + reranker integrate with ES retrieval; Optimize assists with batching, quantization, and prefix caching; Console gives tracing, rollouts, and model pinning; security pack includes SOC2, SAML, KMS details. Next steps: we'll send pilot proposal + pricing, share SOC2 and network diagrams, and schedule an Aug 3rd kickoff if that works.
[12:36] Priya Rao: Aug 3rd is good.
[12:40] Marco Nguyen: One more question — do you have any reference with similar catalog volumes?
[12:45] Maya Chen: We have customers in retail and docs search at similar scale — I'll include anonymized references.
[12:51] [13:00] Liam O'Neill: I'll also run a tailored latency/cost estimate using your 350 qps peak and token distributions and send that in the follow-up.
[13:09] Diana Lopez: We'll compile our compliance checklist and send over to Maya.
[13:13] Maya Chen: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the items listed.
[13:18] [call ends]

Notes on transcript: occasional mislabels and auto-caption errors present (e.g., 'Optimize' heard as 'Optima', 'KV cache' sometimes as 'K-V cache'); speakers occasionally overlap and filler phrases preserved.
